title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
oneLinerQuestion: Find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within a histogram.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Largest Rectangle in Histogram problem asks for the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within a histogram given an array of bar heights. For any given bar, the maximum rectangle using its full height is bounded by the first shorter bar to its left and the first shorter bar to its right. Instead of an O(N^2) brute-force scan to identify these boundaries for every bar, we maintain a Monotonic Increasing Stack of indices. This structure allows us to determine the left and right limiting boundaries for each bar in amortized O(1) time per element.

- Step 1: Stack Definition & Auxiliary Setup — We initialize an empty stack 'stack = []' that will store indices of the histogram bars in strictly increasing order of their heights. We also track 'maxArea = 0'.

- Step 2: Linear Histogram Traversal with Sentinel Boundary — We iterate with pointer 'i' from 0 up to 'heights.length'. When i === heights.length, we treat the current height as 0 (a dummy sentinel value) to force all remaining indices to be popped and processed before completion.

- Step 3: Detecting Shorter Bars & Stack Eviction — While the stack is not empty and the current bar height 'currentHeight = (i === heights.length ? 0 : heights[i])' is strictly less than the height of the bar at the index atop the stack (heights[stack[stack.length - 1]]), the popped bar cannot extend any further to the right. We pop that index: poppedIndex = stack.pop().

- Step 4: Rectangular Area Calculation — For the popped bar, its height is 'h = heights[poppedIndex]'. Its right boundary is 'i' (the current shorter bar), and its left boundary is the new top of the stack (the nearest shorter bar to its left). If the stack is empty, it means this bar was the shortest encountered so far and extends all the way back to index 0: 'width = stack.length === 0 ? i : (i - stack[stack.length - 1] - 1)'. We compute 'area = h * width' and update 'maxArea = Math.max(maxArea, area)'.

- Step 5: Pushing Current Index — Once all taller bars have been evicted and their bounded areas evaluated, we push the current index 'i' onto the monotonic stack.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — After processing the sentinel height at index N, the stack is completely empty, and 'maxArea' contains the largest possible rectangular area contained within the histogram.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because each bar index is pushed onto the stack exactly once and popped at most once during the traversal. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space to store the monotonic stack of indices in the worst-case scenario of strictly increasing heights.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION largestRectangleArea(heights):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK(), maxArea = 0, n = LENGTH(heights)
    FOR i FROM 0 TO n DO:
        h = (i == n) ? 0 : heights[i]
        WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(stack) AND heights[TOP(stack)] > h DO:
            height = heights[POP(stack)]
            width = IS_EMPTY(stack) ? i : i - TOP(stack) - 1
            maxArea = MAX(maxArea, height * width)
        END WHILE
        PUSH i TO stack
    END FOR
    RETURN maxArea
END FUNCTION
